ApprovalStatus.description: Standing of a governed artifact's sign-off, read from its approving Review(s) (§4 spine). Distinct from ThreatModelStatus (the content lifecycle).
ApprovalStatus.title: ApprovalStatus

Assertion.description: Reified edge (§4): subject / predicate / object, so a Review, confidence, and provenance can point at the statement. Substrate-neutral logical node; RDF-star, named graphs, and LPG edge-properties are storage lowerings (ADR-0004) and are not chosen here. Promoting a reviewed edge to this node narrows DEC-004 (no pure edge-property-only form for reviewed assertions). The acceptance gate (provenance + review before status=accepted) is a hand-written constraint, not something gen-shacl emits (§13).

asserted_at.description: Accepted via ADR-0011 (DL-0024). When the statement was made or captured (PROV-O generatedAtTime).

asserted_by.description: Accepted via ADR-0011 (DL-0024). Who made the statement: a person, an organization (a CNA, a scanner vendor's feed) or a software agent (PartyKind `software_agent`). PROV-O wasAttributedTo (proposal §4; DL-0021 finding 4).

assertion_status.description: Proposal status of the Assertion (§4). Must not be `accepted` until provenance and a review are present. That gate is not encoded as a LinkML cardinality rule (§13).

confidence.description: Confidence attached to the Assertion (§4). Scale is not fixed in the proposal.

evidence.description: Accepted via ADR-0011 (DL-0024). Opaque references to what the statement rests on: an SBOM digest, an advisory or CVE record URL, a write-up.

generated_by.description: Accepted via ADR-0011 (DL-0024). The activity that produced the statement, as text: a tool and version, a database build time, a method (PROV-O wasGeneratedBy). Without it the same SBOM gives different answers on different days (RPT-0004 pilot.md §3).

id.description: Stable object id (ADR-0004). Adapters must not renumber it.

predicate.description: Edge type name (§4), e.g. composed_of, affects, realizes, owned_by. Not a closed enum: reviewed edges that are not first-class slots still reify here (including the human-reviewed CWE↔CAPEC mapping, §2).

Assertion.title: Assertion

Asset.description: Accepted via ADR-0011 (DL-0024). Something worth protecting: the thing damage happens to (ARCH-0001 §3). In ISO/SAE 21434 terms (3.1.2, as paraphrased in RPT-0007), it has value and one or more cybersecurity properties whose compromise can lead to a damage scenario. Maps OTM `assets` and threagile data assets. Data, functions and the vehicle itself can all be assets; where an asset lives is `stored_in` / `processed_by`.

id.description: Stable object id (ADR-0004). Adapters must not renumber it.

owned_by.description: Proposal attaches owned_by to Asset (§2b, §3). Asset is not a §13 class; the slot is on Product, ProductInstance, and Component as the structural stand-in. It selects whose business_impact would apply. The business_impact axis itself is post-MVP and has no slot.

processed_by.description: Accepted via ADR-0011 (DL-0024). Components that process the Asset (OTM component `assets.processed`).

security_properties.description: Accepted via ADR-0011 (DL-0024). The cybersecurity properties worth protecting for this Asset.

stored_in.description: Accepted via ADR-0011 (DL-0024). Components that store the Asset (OTM component `assets.stored`).

Asset.title: Asset

AttackPath.description: An ordered set of AttackSteps realising a ThreatInstance (§2a, §3). Feasibility is rated here, at path level (human-rated at MVP). Feasibility METHOD is ISO/SAE 21434 Table-1 (§3, DL-0011), human-rated at MVP; Common Criteria is display-only (numbers + label). No per-step aggregation at MVP. DEC-003 is open; ADR-0005 was dropped, not accepted.

attack_feasibility.description: Path-level feasibility, ISO 21434 4-point scale, human-rated at MVP (§3, Table 1 / RQ-15-10). Not CVSS. Not per-step min/max (that is post-MVP).

id.description: Stable object id (ADR-0004). Adapters must not renumber it.

pivots_to.description: Path-level pivot across a reachability substrate (§1). Reachability's other two levels (connected_via, step preconditions) are not classes in §13.

realizes_threat.description: This path realises the threat scenario (§3).

steps.description: AttackSteps in this path (§2a). Order is the `precedes` edges, not list position.

AttackPath.title: AttackPath

AttackPattern.description: Generic attack pattern (CAPEC / ATT&CK technique = *what*, §1, §2a). STRIDE is not a property of this class (§2). Kill-chain phase is on AttackStep, not here.

catalog_ref.description: External catalog identifier when the proposal names one (CWE, CAPEC, ATT&CK, CVE, D3FEND). The identifier scheme is not pinned in §13.

id.description: Stable object id (ADR-0004). Adapters must not renumber it.

AttackPattern.title: AttackPattern

AttackStep.description: A step in an attack graph (§2a): AND/OR `gate`, explicit `precedes` order, shareable across paths. Optional kill-chain phase is coarse order, not the ATT&CK technique. Pre/postconditions are not given a schema shape in §2a.

gate.description: AND/OR combination of this step with its predecessors (§2a, R-031).

id.description: Stable object id (ADR-0004). Adapters must not renumber it.

kill_chain_phase.description: Optional coarse order tag (§2a). Distinct from the ATT&CK technique. The Lockheed kill-chain record is not pinned; do not rely on a fixed vocabulary.

precedes.description: Explicit ordering edge (§2a). Steps may be shared across paths.

AttackStep.title: AttackStep

Checkpoint.description: A lighter, recurring review point on a SecurityProgram (§3c R-041) — a ProgramNode with no extra shape; it reuses `gated_by` / `decided_by` / `at_phase`. Corporate SDLs name these variously (checkpoint, review, stage).

actual_date.description: Actual date a program node occurred (§3c R-041). Open if not yet reached.

at_phase.description: Canonical LifecyclePhase a program node maps onto (§3b/§3c R-041). Gates are the governance points between phases; `name` is the local corporate label (MAP-0001 gate crosswalk).

decided_by.description: Reviews that decide a program node's passage (§3c R-041). The §4 human-review spine — not a parallel approval mechanism.

depends_on_node.description: Entry-criteria / dependency edges between program nodes (§3c R-041).

gate_status.description: Passage status of a program node (§3c R-041): planned / in-progress / passed / failed / waived / blocked.

gated_by.description: Requirements whose conformance gates passage of this program node (§3c R-041/R-042).

id.description: Stable object id (ADR-0004). Adapters must not renumber it.

order.description: Position of a program node within its SecurityProgram (§3c R-041).

owner.description: Owner/approver of a governed artifact (§3c R-043). A Party ROLE (§2b — one identity, many facets), NOT a new actor type (iteration-7 guardrail, DL-0010).

planned_date.description: Planned date of a program node (§3c R-041 program management).

Checkpoint.title: Checkpoint

Component.description: Authoritative deployed artifact (service, container, dependency, chip, core). Since ADR-0011 it is also the end of a DataFlow and a member of a trust zone, as an OTM component is; the field-level OTM crosswalk stays with #9 (§0). `uses_component` / `composed_of` are the propagation paths for vulnerabilities (§5).

component_kind.description: Accepted via ADR-0011 (DL-0024). What kind of thing a Component is (RPT-0004 Table 6b, 6e; R-022).

composed_of.description: Recursive structural composition (§3). Inlined as references, not as nested trees.

id.description: Stable object id (ADR-0004). Adapters must not renumber it.

identifiers.description: Opaque external / instance-identity strings for a structural node — Product, ProductInstance, or Component (§1). This is ADR-0002's per-type instance identity ("software = a build/commit/hash/SBOM; hardware = firmware + buses + cores (HBOM)") and the generic↔instance half of DEC-009, which the §13 classes otherwise could not carry: `catalog_ref` names a GENERIC catalog entry (CWE/CVE/CAPEC), not the concrete artifact. Scheme-prefixed and OPAQUE, like `catalog_ref` / `external_refs` — a CPE, a package URL (purl), a SWID/SBOM ref, a build/commit hash, or a firmware-image digest. The scheme is NOT pinned and no CPE/SBOM schema is imported (ADR-0004 substrate-neutrality). Additive DRAFT slot (DEC-001 open); not a new §13 class.

in_trust_zone.description: Accepted via ADR-0011 (DL-0024). The trust zone a Component sits in (the proposal's §1 name, F12). One zone per Component, as in OTM; outer zones follow from `within_boundary`.

manufactured_by.description: Relational role edge (§2b), not a classification on Party.

owned_by.description: Proposal attaches owned_by to Asset (§2b, §3). Asset is not a §13 class; the slot is on Product, ProductInstance, and Component as the structural stand-in. It selects whose business_impact would apply. The business_impact axis itself is post-MVP and has no slot.

supplied_by.description: Relational role edge (§2b). The same Party may supply one product and consume another.

uses_component.description: Use edge along which vuln/finding propagation is sound (§5).

version.description: Accepted via ADR-0011 (DL-0024). The version string as the source wrote it (RPT-0004 Table 6b). Until now only the purl inside `identifiers` carried it.

Component.title: Component

ComponentKind.description: Accepted via ADR-0011 (DL-0024). CycloneDX 1.7's thirteen component types, written with underscores, plus `service` (CycloneDX `services[]`) and `interconnect` (a bus or network segment, which the proposal's §1 calls Interconnect and the schema does not model).
ComponentKind.title: ComponentKind

DamageScenario.description: The damage a ThreatInstance realizes (§1). Impact categories are recorded on RiskScore, not collapsed here (§3).

compromised_property.description: Accepted via ADR-0011 (DL-0024). Which cybersecurity property of the damaged Asset is compromised (ISO/SAE 21434 3.1.20, 3.1.33).

damages_asset.description: Accepted via ADR-0011 (DL-0024). The Asset(s) a DamageScenario harms (ISO/SAE 21434 damage scenario; RPT-0007 §1).

id.description: Stable object id (ADR-0004). Adapters must not renumber it.

DamageScenario.title: DamageScenario

DataFlow.description: Accepted via ADR-0011 (DL-0024). A directed flow of data or commands from one Component to another (OTM `dataflows`, threagile communication links, CycloneDX service `data` flows), carrying Assets. ADR-0011 joins Components directly, which is OTM's shape and needs no DFD classes. The proposal's §1 puts DataFlow in a behavioral DFD layer, between Process, DataStore and ExternalEntity elements `realized_by` Components; a later ADR that adds that layer would widen `flow_from` and `flow_to`. Threats on a flow (spoofing, tampering, disclosure) point at it through ThreatInstance.targets_element.

bidirectional.description: Accepted via ADR-0011 (DL-0024). True when the flow runs both ways (OTM `bidirectional`).

carries.description: Accepted via ADR-0011 (DL-0024). Assets the DataFlow carries (threagile data assets sent and received).

crosses_boundary.description: Accepted via ADR-0011 (DL-0024). Trust zones the DataFlow crosses, stated explicitly when zone membership is incomplete.

flow_from.description: Accepted via ADR-0011 (DL-0024). Where the DataFlow starts.

flow_to.description: Accepted via ADR-0011 (DL-0024). Where the DataFlow ends.

id.description: Stable object id (ADR-0004). Adapters must not renumber it.

protocol.description: Accepted via ADR-0011 (DL-0024). The protocol or bus, as text (for example CAN, HTTPS).

DataFlow.title: DataFlow

Deployment.description: A placement of one ProductInstance (§3). Many Deployments per instance; each points at one Environment. Single deployment is the MVP assumption; deployment-relative risk (R-023) is post-MVP.

environment.description: The one Environment for this Deployment (§3).

id.description: Stable object id (ADR-0004). Adapters must not renumber it.

Deployment.title: Deployment

Environment.description: Reusable operational exposure of a running deployment (§3, F9): physical security, connectivity, operational context. Parameterises feasibility's exploitability side only — never impact CIA (F5). Distinct from LifecyclePhase (§3b). The MVP metric runs without requiring this node.

connectivity.description: Environment facet (§3). Feeds attack vector / reachability / window, not impact.

id.description: Stable object id (ADR-0004). Adapters must not renumber it.

physical_security.description: Environment facet (§3). Feeds feasibility exploitability only, post-MVP.

Environment.title: Environment

FeasibilityLevel.description: ISO/SAE 21434 path-level 4-point scale (§3, Table 1). Human-rated at MVP. Not a Common Criteria score and not a CVSS exploitability number.
FeasibilityLevel.title: FeasibilityLevel

Gate.description: A named, ordered, dated DECISION point with exit criteria and an approving Review (§3c R-041). Its exit criterion runs the conformance check (`validates_conformance_of` a ThreatModel): a model is conformant when every in-scope ThreatInstance has an approved, evidenced Mitigation (R-042). The check PROVES linkage + approval, NOT adequacy — the human cybersecurity-assessment judgement stays a human input (CLAUDE.md).

actual_date.description: Actual date a program node occurred (§3c R-041). Open if not yet reached.

at_phase.description: Canonical LifecyclePhase a program node maps onto (§3b/§3c R-041). Gates are the governance points between phases; `name` is the local corporate label (MAP-0001 gate crosswalk).

decided_by.description: Reviews that decide a program node's passage (§3c R-041). The §4 human-review spine — not a parallel approval mechanism.

depends_on_node.description: Entry-criteria / dependency edges between program nodes (§3c R-041).

gate_status.description: Passage status of a program node (§3c R-041): planned / in-progress / passed / failed / waived / blocked.

gated_by.description: Requirements whose conformance gates passage of this program node (§3c R-041/R-042).

id.description: Stable object id (ADR-0004). Adapters must not renumber it.

order.description: Position of a program node within its SecurityProgram (§3c R-041).

owner.description: Owner/approver of a governed artifact (§3c R-043). A Party ROLE (§2b — one identity, many facets), NOT a new actor type (iteration-7 guardrail, DL-0010).

planned_date.description: Planned date of a program node (§3c R-041 program management).

validates_conformance_of.description: The ThreatModel whose conformance this Gate's exit criterion checks (§3c R-042): every in-scope ThreatInstance has an approved, evidenced Mitigation. Proves linkage + approval, NOT adequacy (CLAUDE.md human-judgement rule).

Gate.title: Gate

GateStatus.description: Passage status of an SDL program node — Gate / Milestone / Checkpoint (§3c R-041).
GateStatus.title: GateStatus

GovernedView.description: The governed, persisted subtype of View (§3c R-043). The existing `View` stays the TRANSIENT lens (query/projection, never written back); a GovernedView is the TRACKED artifact — an owned / approved / reproducible snapshot. It keeps View's `projection`/`focus_query` and adds governance: `owner` (Party ROLE, §2b), `revision` (the saved view's version), approval via the Review spine (`approved_by`) pinned to an `approval_digest` so the sign-off is reproducible against KG state at a point in time (SysML v2 View/Viewpoint, OMG SACM, OSCAL→Word prior art), `governance_status`, and `supersedes`. `renders` the KG scope it materializes (e.g. a ThreatModel or SecurityProgram). Post-MVP.

approval_digest.description: Commit/content digest the approval is pinned to, so the sign-off is REPRODUCIBLE against KG state at a point in time (§3c R-043; SysML v2 View/Viewpoint, OMG SACM, OSCAL→Word prior art). Opaque string; digest scheme not pinned here.

approval_status.description: Standing of the current sign-off, read from the approving Review(s) (§4 spine). Distinct from `governance_status` (where the snapshot is in its life): this tracks the verdict of its review cycle. Denormalized convenience — the authoritative verdict is the Review, not this field.

approved_by.description: Approving Review(s) of a governed artifact (§3c R-043). Approval runs through the existing Review + Assertion spine (§4) — NOT a parallel provenance mechanism (iteration-7 guardrail, DL-0010).

created.description: When the governed artifact was created (§3c R-043 change tracking).

focus_query.description: Bounded query / filter that defines the view (§10, R-033). Opaque to this schema (not a committed query language — DEC-004 is open).

governance_status.description: Lifecycle of a governed snapshot (§3c R-043): draft → in-review → approved → superseded. The shared governed-view lifecycle (named for the ThreatModel case; reused by SecurityProgram and GovernedView).

id.description: Stable object id (ADR-0004). Adapters must not renumber it.

owner.description: Owner/approver of a governed artifact (§3c R-043). A Party ROLE (§2b — one identity, many facets), NOT a new actor type (iteration-7 guardrail, DL-0010).

projection.description: Which derived projection this View spec names (§10).

renders.description: The KG scope a GovernedView materializes (§3c R-043) — e.g. a ThreatModel or SecurityProgram. Content derives from KG state; never written back.

revision.description: Monotonic revision/version of a governed snapshot (§3c R-043). This is the saved view's "version"; ThreatModel and SecurityProgram name the same field `revision`. Tracked across review cycles via `supersedes`.

supersedes.description: The prior revision of this governed snapshot it replaces (§3c R-043).

updated.description: When the governed artifact was last updated (§3c R-043 change tracking).

GovernedView.title: GovernedView

ImpactSeverity.description: ISO 21434 impact ordinal per S/F/O/P category (§3, RQ-15-04/05).
ImpactSeverity.title: ImpactSeverity

ImpactVector.description: Inlined value object for RiskScore.impact (§3). ISO 21434 safety / financial / operational / privacy, each severe|major|moderate|negligible. Keeping the four categories is the method; collapsing to one number is display-only. Not a §13 domain class. business_impact is a different post-MVP axis and is not a field here.

financial.description: Financial impact on the end-beneficiary, not the owner's P&L (§3).

privacy.description: Privacy impact (§3). Not re-indexed by asset owner.

ImpactVector.title: ImpactVector

LifecyclePhase.description: Coarse lifecycle stage (§3b). The vocabulary is LifecyclePhaseCode (concept through decommission/disposal, ISO 21434 + ISO 26262 aligned). Reverse-logistics transitions and custody provenance are post-MVP and are not modeled. `name` is the human label; `code` is the enum.

id.description: Stable object id (ADR-0004). Adapters must not renumber it.

LifecyclePhase.title: LifecyclePhase

LifecyclePhaseCode.description: LifecyclePhase vocabulary (§3b), aligned to ISO/SAE 21434 + ISO 26262. Returns/refurbish/resale/dispose are called out as future phase tags; they are not given codes here because §3b says the returns branch is post-MVP.
LifecyclePhaseCode.title: LifecyclePhaseCode

MethodFacet.description: Method that proposed a ThreatInstance (§2). Only STRIDE is in MVP.
MethodFacet.title: MethodFacet

Milestone.description: A dated, owned deliverable point on a SecurityProgram (§3c R-041), optionally dated relative to another node (`offset_from`). May serve as a gate entry condition via another node's `depends_on_node`.

actual_date.description: Actual date a program node occurred (§3c R-041). Open if not yet reached.

at_phase.description: Canonical LifecyclePhase a program node maps onto (§3b/§3c R-041). Gates are the governance points between phases; `name` is the local corporate label (MAP-0001 gate crosswalk).

decided_by.description: Reviews that decide a program node's passage (§3c R-041). The §4 human-review spine — not a parallel approval mechanism.

depends_on_node.description: Entry-criteria / dependency edges between program nodes (§3c R-041).

gate_status.description: Passage status of a program node (§3c R-041): planned / in-progress / passed / failed / waived / blocked.

gated_by.description: Requirements whose conformance gates passage of this program node (§3c R-041/R-042).

id.description: Stable object id (ADR-0004). Adapters must not renumber it.

offset_from.description: Another program node this Milestone is dated relative to (§3c R-041).

order.description: Position of a program node within its SecurityProgram (§3c R-041).

owner.description: Owner/approver of a governed artifact (§3c R-043). A Party ROLE (§2b — one identity, many facets), NOT a new actor type (iteration-7 guardrail, DL-0010).

planned_date.description: Planned date of a program node (§3c R-041 program management).

Milestone.title: Milestone

Mitigation.description: A mitigation/control (catalog example D3FEND, §1). §5 instance fields (implementation owner, external work-item refs, status) are on this class until a separate MitigationInstance class is accepted. Status is also surfaced as RiskScore.mitigation_status (R-045) — a peer of the derived risk, not an input to it. A GENERIC mitigation for a product type/family is `stated_as` a Requirement (technical, process, audit, …); a product-specific mitigation discharges that Requirement through `Requirement.satisfied_by` (ADR-0012).

applies_in_phase.description: Coarse lifecycle stage a threat or mitigation belongs to (§3b). Not a substitute for Environment. One threat uses the axis that fits.

catalog_ref.description: External catalog identifier when the proposal names one (CWE, CAPEC, ATT&CK, CVE, D3FEND). The identifier scheme is not pinned in §13.

external_refs.description: Linked work items, e.g. a Jira key (§5). Opaque strings; no tracker schema.

id.description: Stable object id (ADR-0004). Adapters must not renumber it.

mitigates.description: Threats this mitigation addresses (§5). Phase binding is applies_in_phase.

mitigation_status.description: Lifecycle of the mitigation (§3 R-045, §5): planned / in-progress / complete / accepted-risk / n-a. Vocabulary may be refined by DEC-009. On RiskScore this is a peer column of feasibility and impact, not folded into `risk`.

stated_as.description: A generic Mitigation (for a product type/family) expressed as a Requirement (ADR-0012). The Requirement carries the family scope and is discharged by product-specific Mitigations via `satisfied_by`. An AI-proposed link is a `proposed` Assertion with predicate `stated_as` until reviewed.

Mitigation.title: Mitigation

MitigationStatus.description: Mitigation lifecycle (§3 R-045). Refined later by DEC-009.
MitigationStatus.title: MitigationStatus

Node.description: Shared identity for every §13 class. `id` is the stable object id ADR-0004 requires across file, LPG, and RDF encodings. Not itself a §13 class.

id.description: Stable object id (ADR-0004). Adapters must not renumber it.

Node.title: Node

Normativity.description: How binding a Requirement is (§3c R-044). A MAP-0001 cell means different things per framework (hard requirement vs maturity activity vs recommendation).
Normativity.title: Normativity

Party.description: One reusable identity for an organization or a person (§2b). ThreatActor and PROV Agent are facets of this identity, not separate §13 classes. Only intrinsic classifications live on the node; supplier/owner/vendor-of are edges.

classifications.description: Intrinsic classifications only, e.g. standards-body, cna (§2b). On a Product, the product types / families it belongs to, scheme-prefixed (e.g. `family:connected-ecu`); `Requirement.applies_to_family` matches these (ADR-0012).

id.description: Stable object id (ADR-0004). Adapters must not renumber it.

Party.title: Party

PartyKind.description: Party is an organization or a person (§2b).
PartyKind.title: PartyKind

Product.description: A product design (structural layer, §1). Recursive composition is `composed_of` Components (§3). There is no ProductFamily class (DEC-009).

ProductInstance.description: A versioned, identity-bearing instance of a Product (§1, §3b). Lifecycle *state* sits here (with valid_from/valid_to), not on Product or Component. A refurbished unit can share a firmware hash and still carry a new phase, Deployment, and owner. The firmware image digest / build hash is an opaque `identifiers` string (ADR-0002 per-type instance identity), not a pinned slot.

build_composed_of.description: Accepted via ADR-0011 (DL-0024). The Components one build contains, as an SBOM lists them (RPT-0004 Table 6c, pilot finding 1). `composed_of` stays the design-level composition on Product and Component; this is the per-build list, which differs between builds of one Product.

current_phase.description: Lifecycle state of this ProductInstance at valid_from/valid_to (§3b).

id.description: Stable object id (ADR-0004). Adapters must not renumber it.

This is ADR-0002's per-type instance identity ("software = a build/commit/hash/SBOM; hardware = firmware + buses + cores (HBOM)") and the generic↔instance half of DEC-009, which the §13 classes otherwise could not carry: `catalog_ref` names a GENERIC catalog entry (CWE/CVE/CAPEC), not the concrete artifact. valid_from.description: Start of the (ProductInstance, time) state interval (§3b). Temporal axis was flagged as still-missing; included here because §3b says to add it with lifecycle state.

valid_to.description: End of the (ProductInstance, time) state interval (§3b). Open-ended if absent.

version.description: Accepted via ADR-0011 (DL-0024). The version string as the source wrote it (RPT-0004 Table 6b). Until now only the purl inside `identifiers` carried it.

ProgramNode.description: Shared shape for an SDL program node (§3c R-041): a named, `order`-ed, dated governance point on a SecurityProgram, mapped onto the LifecyclePhase axis (§3b, `at_phase`). Carries program-management fields — `order`, `planned_date` vs `actual_date`, `gate_status`, `owner` (Party ROLE, §2b), the Requirements that gate passage (`gated_by`), the Reviews that decide it (`decided_by` — the §4 human-review spine, not a parallel mechanism), and node dependencies / entry criteria (`depends_on_node`). Corporate gate-naming varies, so `name` is the local label and `at_phase` the canonical mapping (MAP-0001 gate crosswalk). Not instantiated directly; use Gate / Milestone / Checkpoint.

actual_date.description: Actual date a program node occurred (§3c R-041). Open if not yet reached.

at_phase.description: Canonical LifecyclePhase a program node maps onto (§3b/§3c R-041). Gates are the governance points between phases; `name` is the local corporate label (MAP-0001 gate crosswalk).

decided_by.description: Reviews that decide a program node's passage (§3c R-041). The §4 human-review spine — not a parallel approval mechanism.

depends_on_node.description: Entry-criteria / dependency edges between program nodes (§3c R-041).

gate_status.description: Passage status of a program node (§3c R-041): planned / in-progress / passed / failed / waived / blocked.

gated_by.description: Requirements whose conformance gates passage of this program node (§3c R-041/R-042).

id.description: Stable object id (ADR-0004). Adapters must not renumber it.

order.description: Position of a program node within its SecurityProgram (§3c R-041).

owner.description: Owner/approver of a governed artifact (§3c R-043). A Party ROLE (§2b — one identity, many facets), NOT a new actor type (iteration-7 guardrail, DL-0010).

planned_date.description: Planned date of a program node (§3c R-041 program management).

ProgramNode.title: ProgramNode

RedundancyGroup.description: Marks Deployments (or whole build/review systems) as replicas (§3, §10): `replica_of` / `redundant_with`. Supports common-mode risk and per-replica mitigation divergence. Post-MVP (R-034).

id.description: Stable object id (ADR-0004). Adapters must not renumber it.

RedundancyGroup.title: RedundancyGroup

Requirement.description: CORE (ADR-0012, amending ADR-0010 / DEC-001a). A normative statement a product must meet: taken from a standard, regulation or guideline (ISO/SAE 21434, ETSI EN 304 223, NIST SP 800-218, …) or authored for a product type/family. `text` is the statement and `text_origin` says whether it is a paraphrase, verbatim or authored; for a licensed standard it is ALWAYS a paraphrase and the clause is in `source_locator`. `source_ref` is an OPAQUE uriorcurie into the library requirement record (Threat-Radar/library) — tmodel aligns by reference ONLY; it does not import or depend on the library schema. `requirement_kind` classifies it (technical / process / audit / documentation / organizational / other) and `normativity` says how binding it is. Edges: `refines` / `derived_from` / `conflicts_with` / `maps_to` (overlap, the MAP-0001 crosswalk) to other Requirements; `addresses` the ThreatInstance / Weakness / AttackPattern it counters; `satisfied_by` the Mitigation(s) that discharge it; `applies_to` a Product / ProductInstance / Component, or `applies_to_family` a product type/family (matched against Product.classifications). A generic Mitigation is `stated_as` a Requirement. AI-proposed requirement links are `proposed` Assertions until a human Review accepts them (§4). `conformance_status` is NOT accepted: it is the DEC-001b R-042 verdict (C1) and stays proposal-level; core vectors do not set it.

addresses.description: The ThreatInstance, Weakness or AttackPattern this Requirement counters (ADR-0012). An AI-proposed `addresses` link is a `proposed` Assertion, not a value of this slot, until a human Review accepts it.

applies_to.description: The Product, ProductInstance or Component this Requirement applies to (ADR-0012).

applies_to_family.description: Product type / family scope (ADR-0012), as an opaque scheme-prefixed value matched against `Product.classifications`, e.g. `family:connected-ecu`. Used instead of a ProductFamily class, which DEC-009 has not decided.

conflicts_with.description: The two Requirements cannot both be met as written; a human must resolve it (ADR-0012). Symmetric in meaning; record it on either side.

conformance_status.description: PROPOSED (DEC-001b, not accepted by ADR-0012). Automatable R-042 conformance verdict for a Requirement: whether it has an approved, evidenced mitigation. Proves linkage + approval, NOT adequacy. Core (mvp-*) vectors do not set it.

derived_from.description: This Requirement was derived from the target (e.g. a product requirement derived from a standard's provision, ISO/SAE 21434 RQ-09-09). Unlike `refines`, the intent may differ (ADR-0012).

id.description: Stable object id (ADR-0004). Adapters must not renumber it.

maps_to.description: Overlap / cross-spec crosswalk edge (§3c R-044) = the MAP-0001 overlap: the two Requirements ask for substantially the same thing. Reviewed mappings reify as Assertions (§4) so they can carry provenance + a Review.

normativity.description: How binding a Requirement is (§3c R-044): mandatory / recommended / optional / informative / conditional. MAP-0001 shows a cell means different things per framework (hard requirement vs maturity activity vs recommendation).

refines.description: This Requirement makes the target more specific for a product, family or component (same intent, narrower scope or more detail) (ADR-0012).

requirement_kind.description: What kind of obligation a Requirement is (ADR-0012).

satisfied_by.description: Mitigation(s) that discharge this Requirement (ADR-0012; §3c R-042). Normally product-specific mitigations; the generic family mitigation is linked the other way, by `Mitigation.stated_as`.

source_locator.description: Human-readable clause / section / table locator in the source, e.g. `RQ-09-09 (§9.5.2)` or `Provision 5.2.1` (ADR-0012). With a paraphrased `text` this is how a reader finds the authoritative wording.

source_ref.description: OPAQUE reference to the library record (Threat-Radar/library) the Requirement comes from, scheme-prefixed like `catalog_ref`, e.g. `library:iso-sae-21434-2021#RQ-09-09` (ADR-0012; §3c R-044, §2b). tmodel aligns by reference — it does NOT import or depend on the library schema. Absent for a project-authored requirement.

text.description: The normative statement of a Requirement (ADR-0012; §3c R-044). Distinct from `description`. For a licensed standard (ISO, IEC, SAE) it is a paraphrase, never the standard's wording; `text_origin` records which.

text_origin.description: Whether `text` is a paraphrase of the source, the source's own words (only where the source's licence allows it), or authored by the project (ADR-0012).

Requirement.title: Requirement

RequirementConformanceStatus.description: Automatable R-042 conformance verdict for a Requirement — linkage + approval, NOT adequacy (the human cybersecurity-assessment role remains, CLAUDE.md).
RequirementConformanceStatus.title: RequirementConformanceStatus

RequirementKind.description: What kind of obligation a Requirement is (ADR-0012). A mitigation that becomes a requirement can be any of these, not only technical.
RequirementKind.title: RequirementKind

Review.description: Human verdict on an Assertion (§4, §5). Kept separate from the proposal. Carries status, priority, and justification. STIX Opinion/Note is a future mapping (DEC-002 / #9), not a parent class.

id.description: Stable object id (ADR-0004). Adapters must not renumber it.

justification.description: Why the verdict was reached (§5). Separate from the Assertion text.

priority.description: Review priority (§5). Scale not specified in the proposal.

review_status.description: Verdict status (§5). Kept open: proposal does not enumerate the values.

reviewer.description: Human (or, later, an agent facet of a Party) who issued the verdict (§4).

Review.title: Review

RiskScore.description: Composite risk vector (sponsor round, proposed.10 / DL-0011; DEC-003 OPEN — ADR-0005 was dropped, not accepted). Peer slots: feasibility (ISO 21434 Table-1 method; Common Criteria display-only — numbers, label, and a colored indicator in table views), impact (from attack damage; 21434 S/F/O/P), mitigation_status, and derived risk. Shown alongside its inputs, never instead of them. Not a single CVSS score. More components only with a further sponsor decision. MVP: one stakeholder; business_impact is post-MVP and intentionally has no slot.

attack_paths.description: Paths whose feasibilities feed this score. Reduction across paths is worst-path (§3); this schema stores the set, not the fold function.

damage_scenario.description: Damage scenario whose impact feeds M(I, F) (§3).

feasibility.description: Vector component (§3, DL-0011). Copied or reduced from AttackPath.attack_feasibility (worst path). Method is ISO 21434 Table-1, not Common Criteria.

for_stakeholder.description: Owner this score is reported for, when a path crosses assets with different owners (§3). MVP assumes one stakeholder; omit unless needed.

id.description: Stable object id (ADR-0004). Adapters must not renumber it.

impact.description: Per-category S/F/O/P vector (§3). Human-supplied. Do not replace this object with a single severity.

mitigation_status.description: Lifecycle of the mitigation (§3 R-045, §5): planned / in-progress / complete / accepted-risk / n-a. Vocabulary may be refined by DEC-009. On RiskScore this is a peer column of feasibility and impact, not folded into `risk`.

risk.description: Derived Risk = M(Impact, Feasibility) (§3). ISO 21434 wants one value 1–5 per (threat-scenario, impact-category), and per stakeholder when owners differ. Stored as text because the aggregation function is not fixed until a DEC-003 ADR. Not a CVSS base score. Display may add a colour and a feasibility label; that styling is not a slot.

threat.description: Threat scenario this score is about (§3, RQ-15-15/16).

RiskScore.title: RiskScore

SecurityProgram.description: The SDL as a first-class, GOVERNED, VERSIONED object (§3c R-041). An ordered, named, dated program `governs` a Product / ProductInstance / ProductFamily and is composed of `program_nodes` (Gate / Milestone / Checkpoint) mapped onto the LifecyclePhase axis (§3b, each node's `at_phase`). It `incorporates` the Requirements it enforces; its gates run the conformance check (R-042). Full program management lives on the program nodes (owner, planned/actual dates, status per node). It is itself a governed view (owner / revision / approved_by + approval_digest / governance_status / supersedes), reconciling §10 "views are transient": the SDL plan is a named, versioned, signed-off snapshot over the one SoT, iterating across review cycles. Post-MVP.

approval_digest.description: Commit/content digest the approval is pinned to, so the sign-off is REPRODUCIBLE against KG state at a point in time (§3c R-043; SysML v2 View/Viewpoint, OMG SACM, OSCAL→Word prior art). Opaque string; digest scheme not pinned here.

approval_status.description: Standing of the current sign-off, read from the approving Review(s) (§4 spine). Distinct from `governance_status` (where the snapshot is in its life): this tracks the verdict of its review cycle. Denormalized convenience — the authoritative verdict is the Review, not this field.

approved_by.description: Approving Review(s) of a governed artifact (§3c R-043). Approval runs through the existing Review + Assertion spine (§4) — NOT a parallel provenance mechanism (iteration-7 guardrail, DL-0010).

created.description: When the governed artifact was created (§3c R-043 change tracking).

governance_status.description: Lifecycle of a governed snapshot (§3c R-043): draft → in-review → approved → superseded. The shared governed-view lifecycle (named for the ThreatModel case; reused by SecurityProgram and GovernedView).

governs.description: The Product / ProductInstance / ProductFamily a SecurityProgram is attached to (§3c R-041). Range Node: ProductFamily is not a §13 class.

id.description: Stable object id (ADR-0004). Adapters must not renumber it.

owner.description: Owner/approver of a governed artifact (§3c R-043). A Party ROLE (§2b — one identity, many facets), NOT a new actor type (iteration-7 guardrail, DL-0010).

program_nodes.description: Ordered Gate / Milestone / Checkpoint nodes of a SecurityProgram (§3c R-041). Order is each node's `order`, not list position.

revision.description: Monotonic revision/version of a governed snapshot (§3c R-043). This is the saved view's "version"; ThreatModel and SecurityProgram name the same field `revision`. Tracked across review cycles via `supersedes`.

supersedes.description: The prior revision of this SDL program it replaces (§3c R-041/R-043).

updated.description: When the governed artifact was last updated (§3c R-043 change tracking).

SecurityProgram.title: SecurityProgram

SecurityProperty.description: Accepted via ADR-0011 (DL-0024). Cybersecurity properties (ISO/SAE 21434 3.1.20 names confidentiality, integrity and availability as examples). The other three follow the STRIDE sketch `violates_property` already uses (authentication, authorization, non-repudiation), with authenticity as the property of data that authentication protects.
SecurityProperty.title: SecurityProperty

ThreatInstance.description: A threat in a model, not the generic catalog entry (§1). Carries the method facet (STRIDE and, post-MVP, LINDDUN/MAESTRO) and `realizes` a DamageScenario. Phase scope is `applies_in_phase` (§3b), distinct from Environment.

applies_in_phase.description: Coarse lifecycle stage a threat or mitigation belongs to (§3b). Not a substitute for Environment. One threat uses the axis that fits.

id.description: Stable object id (ADR-0004). Adapters must not renumber it.

method_facet.description: Which method classified this threat (§2). STRIDE is a facet, not an AttackPattern property. Facets beyond STRIDE are post-MVP.

targets_element.description: Accepted via ADR-0011 (DL-0024). The element a ThreatInstance acts on: a Component, a DataFlow, an Asset or a TrustBoundary, as OTM attaches threats to components and data flows and STRIDE classifies per DFD element (RPT-0015 §4 notes ThreatInstance has no `targets` or `on_element` edge).

violates_property.description: Security property the facet says is violated (§2). STRIDE sketch, not a closed enum: S authentication, T integrity, R non-repudiation, I confidentiality, D availability, E authorization.

ThreatInstance.title: ThreatInstance

ThreatModel.description: A GOVERNED, VERSIONED view/snapshot over the KG-as-SoT (§3c R-043). NOT domain truth re-stated: a reviewed LENS whose membership and verdicts are tracked across review cycles. Scope is either a bounded `scope_query` or an explicit `members` set (in-scope ThreatInstances / AttackPaths / Components / Products). Governance is the shared governed-view facet: `owner` (a Party ROLE, §2b — not a new actor type), `revision`, approval through the existing Review spine (`approved_by`) pinned to an `approval_digest` so sign-off is REPRODUCIBLE against KG state at a point in time, `governance_status` (draft/in-review/approved/superseded), and `supersedes` the prior revision. ARCH-0001 has no ThreatModel class; this is the scope node for "the threat model itself" (RPT-0013-OM §2). Post-MVP as an SDL object (the threat content it scopes is MVP).

approval_digest.description: Commit/content digest the approval is pinned to, so the sign-off is REPRODUCIBLE against KG state at a point in time (§3c R-043; SysML v2 View/Viewpoint, OMG SACM, OSCAL→Word prior art). Opaque string; digest scheme not pinned here.

approval_status.description: Standing of the current sign-off, read from the approving Review(s) (§4 spine). Distinct from `governance_status` (where the snapshot is in its life): this tracks the verdict of its review cycle. Denormalized convenience — the authoritative verdict is the Review, not this field.

approved_by.description: Approving Review(s) of a governed artifact (§3c R-043). Approval runs through the existing Review + Assertion spine (§4) — NOT a parallel provenance mechanism (iteration-7 guardrail, DL-0010).

created.description: When the governed artifact was created (§3c R-043 change tracking).

governance_status.description: Lifecycle of a governed snapshot (§3c R-043): draft → in-review → approved → superseded. The shared governed-view lifecycle (named for the ThreatModel case; reused by SecurityProgram and GovernedView).

id.description: Stable object id (ADR-0004). Adapters must not renumber it.

members.description: Explicit in-scope members of a ThreatModel snapshot (§3c R-043): ThreatInstances, AttackPaths, Components, Products. References, not copies — membership is a reviewed lens over the KG, never domain truth re-stated.

owner.description: Owner/approver of a governed artifact (§3c R-043). A Party ROLE (§2b — one identity, many facets), NOT a new actor type (iteration-7 guardrail, DL-0010).

revision.description: Monotonic revision/version of a governed snapshot (§3c R-043). This is the saved view's "version"; ThreatModel and SecurityProgram name the same field `revision`. Tracked across review cycles via `supersedes`.

scope_query.description: Bounded query/filter defining a ThreatModel snapshot's membership (§3c R-043). Opaque to this schema (DEC-004 open), like View.focus_query. Use `members` for an explicit set instead.

supersedes.description: The prior revision of this threat-model snapshot it replaces (§3c R-043).

updated.description: When the governed artifact was last updated (§3c R-043 change tracking).

ThreatModel.title: ThreatModel

ThreatModelStatus.description: Lifecycle of a governed snapshot (§3c R-043). Named for the ThreatModel case; the same lifecycle is reused by SecurityProgram and GovernedView.
ThreatModelStatus.title: ThreatModelStatus

TrustBoundary.description: Accepted via ADR-0011 (DL-0024). Where control or assumptions change (ARCH-0001 §3), modeled as a zone, as the proposal's §1 does: a Component is `in_trust_zone` a TrustBoundary (§1, F12), and zones nest through `within_boundary`, which can also name the Component a zone sits inside, because an OTM trust zone's `parent` may be a component. A DataFlow whose ends sit in different zones crosses the boundary between them; `crosses_boundary` states it explicitly where membership is unknown. Maps OTM `trustZones` and pytm boundaries; threagile's member lists and CycloneDX's per-service `trustZone` import onto the same zone (RPT-0005 crosswalk, "four shapes"). `zone_type` and `trust_level` keep the source's own labels.

id.description: Stable object id (ADR-0004). Adapters must not renumber it.

trust_level.description: Accepted via ADR-0011 (DL-0024). The zone's trust rating as the source gives it (OTM `trustRating`); not normalized here.

within_boundary.description: Accepted via ADR-0011 (DL-0024). What encloses the zone: another trust zone, for nesting (pytm boundaries nest), or a Component, since an OTM trust zone's `parent` may point at a component as well as at a zone.

zone_type.description: Accepted via ADR-0011 (DL-0024). The zone's type as the source gives it (OTM `trustZones[].type`; threagile's trust boundaries are typed too); not normalized here.

TrustBoundary.title: TrustBoundary

View.description: Derived presentation lens (§10): query/filter + projection. Not domain truth and never written back onto domain nodes. Saved views may be persisted; rendered geometry is transient and out of this schema. One graph projection is MVP; other projections are post-MVP.

focus_query.description: Bounded query / filter that defines the view (§10, R-033). Opaque to this schema (not a committed query language — DEC-004 is open).

id.description: Stable object id (ADR-0004). Adapters must not renumber it.

projection.description: Which derived projection this View spec names (§10).

View.title: View

ViewProjection.description: Named projections over one graph (§10). Matrix, compare, saved views are post-MVP.
ViewProjection.title: ViewProjection

Vulnerability.description: A finding/vulnerability (CVE/NVD-shaped) that `affects` a Product (§2b). Propagation along uses_component/composed_of and the per-instance VEX override are Assertions plus Reviews (§5), not extra classes.

alias_ids.description: Accepted via ADR-0011 (DL-0024). Other ids of the same Vulnerability (GHSA, OSV, distribution advisories); `catalog_ref` keeps the primary id (RPT-0004 Table 6d).

assigned_by.description: Assigning CNA (§2b). Party.classifications should include cna when this is set; not enforced here.

catalog_ref.description: External catalog identifier when the proposal names one (CWE, CAPEC, ATT&CK, CVE, D3FEND). The identifier scheme is not pinned in §13.

id.description: Stable object id (ADR-0004). Adapters must not renumber it.

instance_of.description: Accepted via ADR-0011 (DL-0024). The Weakness (CWE) a Vulnerability is an instance of (ARCH-0001 §3 `instance_of`; PLAN-0002 §5). Who assigned it (CNA, ADP, NVD) is not a property of this edge: keep it on an Assertion with `asserted_by` (RPT-0004 rule R-CWE-1).

Vulnerability.title: Vulnerability

Weakness.description: Generic weakness, catalogued as CWE (§1 layer 3). The CWE↔CAPEC link is a human-reviewed mapping (an Assertion), not a facet property (§2) — no hard edge to AttackPattern in this cut.

catalog_ref.description: External catalog identifier when the proposal names one (CWE, CAPEC, ATT&CK, CVE, D3FEND). The identifier scheme is not pinned in §13.

id.description: Stable object id (ADR-0004). Adapters must not renumber it.

Weakness.title: Weakness
